messages:
maria: quick heads-up — I'm starting an onboarding run for aurora-v2 (35B) into the canary pool, placing weights under s3://redwood-models/aurora-v2/weights-v3. prefetched KV cache enabled to test sliding-window perf. noticed two things so far :eyes:

aj: thanks for the ping. can you paste the exact tokenizer file you used? last time we hit odd utf-8 continuation bytes that messed up RoPE offsets.

maria: yep — using tokenizer at s3://redwood-models/aurora-v2/tokenizer/tokenizer.json. quick diff showed some added normalizers: "strip_combining": true. also found tokens with leading 0xC2 sequence when converting legacy bpe -> json.

samir: 0xC2 usually indicates an encoding mismatch. try running `python -c "open('tokenizer.json','rb').read()[:64]"` and check for non-utf8 sequences. if present, the byte offsets for RoPE can shift.

lee: fwiw, we saw a similar symptom where RoPE scale mismatch manifested as trailing garbage tokens when using Triton kernels vs native torch. are you running the GQA or MQA variant?

maria: canary config is MQA enabled (sharded kv across heads) — config snippet I used:

```json
{
  "model": "aurora-v2",
  "quant_mode": "int8",
  "gqa": false,
  "mqa": true,
  "rope_scale": 1.0,
  "sliding_window": {
    "enabled": true,
    "window_size": 2048,
    "prefetch_kv": true
  }
}
```

nina: interesting — rope_scale=1.0 might be wrong for this checkpoint. upstream export included a rope_scale of 1.024 in the metadata (weird). can you cat the model_metadata.json under the weights path?

maria: grabbed it, here's the line: "rope_scale": 1.024. I had assumed default 1.0 — my bad.

aj: that would definitely shift positional embeddings between runtime implementations. update the config to rope_scale: 1.024 and rerun quick decode checks. also re-generate the tokenizer from the binary export with `tokenizer-cli normalize --strict` to strip stray bytes.

maria: re-ran with rope_scale: 1.024 and normalized tokenizer. immediate improvement in perplexity on the smoke prompt. still seeing occasional mismatch between Triton and CPU kernels at token 128/129 for some inputs.

samir: token boundary mismatch usually traces back to either (a) tokenizer differences, (b) KV prefetch race, or (c) attention mask shape mismatch when sliding window boundary is crossed. since you enabled prefetched KV, can you try toggling `prefetch_kv: false` to see if it reproduces?

maria: toggled prefetch_kv=false, re-ran — Triton and CPU outputs align now. score drop negligible but latency up ~12%.

lee: good repro. that suggests a synchronization/ordering bug in the prefetch path for MQA. tagging infra-bot for a canary rollout hold and samir for a small patch. @infra-bot can we hold canary?

infra-bot: incident: canary rollouts paused for aurora-v2/weights-v3 per request from eng-runtime at 2209876721. assigned to samir.

samir: I'll push a small fix to ensure KV prefetch awaits the first attention op and add an assert for expected kv shapes when sliding_window boundary crosses. will open a PR and request review from @lee and @aj. ETA ~2h.

aj: ping me on the PR, will do a quick kernel-level review. also we should add a regression test: decode with prefetch on/off and assert identical tokens up to 512.

maria: thanks — I'll hold further canaries until patch lands. leaving notes in the onboarding checklist: weights path, tokenizer normalization, rope_scale mismatch, prefetched-kv race. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: canary status: paused for aurora-v2 (weights-v3). awaiting human clearance.

nina: re: tokenizer quirks — I can help add a small CI job that validates tokenizer bytes and compares tokenization against the legacy export. that'll catch 0xC2/0xA0 anomalies before onboarding.

maria: awesome. will add that to the onboarding checklist and post the PR link when samir opens it. thanks all. :party-popper:
